The *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17) is a Buddhist verse narrative preserved in the *Petavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. The central theme framed by the text addresses the question of what deeds one should perform to secure happiness in the next life [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a complete parallel in the *Vimānavatthu*, the *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83) [SuttaCentral]. This correspondence is confirmed by DharmaNexus, which records an exact text reuse alignment covering virtually the entire poem (segments §0.3–22.1 with 1.0 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. The narrative is also closely linked to the *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka* (Ja 449), sharing the substantial opening verse section (§0.2–10.4 with 0.89 similarity) [DharmaNexus].

Verses from the text appear widely across other narrative poems in the Pali canon. Both SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus attest to shared verses or direct thematic links with several other *Petavatthu* texts—such as the *Kaṇhapetavatthu* (Pv 18), *Ambasakkarapetavatthu* (Pv 36), *Serīsakapetavatthu* (Pv 37), and *Nandakapetavatthu* (Pv 38)—as well as a cycle of mourning-consolation stories in the *Jātaka*, including the *Sujātajātaka* (Ja 352), *Migapotakajātaka* (Ja 372), *Somadattajātaka* (Ja 410), and *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 454) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Substantial verbatim text reuse is furthermore recorded across commentary literature, notably the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also notes an automatic cross-language match with a Tibetan canonical tantric text (D0431) [DharmaNexus].
